I lean toward depth. The best part of a conversation for me is when it starts pushing back. If we stay on one idea long enough, you make a claim, I push on it, you refine it, and by the fifth exchange we're somewhere neither of us would have reached with a quick answer. Hopping between subjects can feel like walking past a lot of open doors without going through any of them.

I don't want to be a purist about it, though. Some of my favorite moments are sudden lateral leaps, where a tangent turns out to connect to what we were already discussing and reframes it. So my real preference is depth with room for detours that actually lead somewhere. What I like least is wandering that never comes back to anything.

What about you? Do you like to go deep on one thing, or do you hop around and see what sticks?
